prompts.evidence: Fails supported_by_section. Idea 1 (each light has its own pattern and sailors count the flashes): d02-p006, 'every light on the coast had its own pattern, and that sailors counted the flashes'. Idea 2 (Gannet Rock's pattern is unique): d02-p006, 'one white flash every ten seconds; no other light on the coast did the same'. Unsupported claim: 'made by a lens with four bright panels that turned once every forty seconds'. No paragraph of section s0001 states this; d02-p005 describes the lens only as 'rings of cut glass that bent the light of a single oil flame into one narrow beam'. The four panels and the forty-second turn are in d02-p008, section s0002 ('the gears turned the lens once every forty seconds, and its four bright panels gave four flashes on each turn'). The prompt itself is answerable from d02-p006 and does not telegraph the answer.

Idea 1 (he steered by the horn's sound alone, following its pattern): d03-p009, 'He had steered by the sound of the horn alone— two blasts, then silence, then two blasts again'. Idea 2 (until the boat grounded below the tower): d03-p009, 'until his boat grounded on the shingle below the tower'. The prompt mentions the fog but not the horn, so it does not give the answer away.

Idea 1 (the glow is phosphorescence, light from tiny living creatures when water is disturbed): d03-p010, 'phosphorescence, the light made by tiny living creatures when the water is disturbed'. Idea 2 (not dangerous, a sign of plankton and therefore fish): d03-p011, 'It was not, said Dr. Vane, but it was a sign that the water was full of plankton, and where there was plankton there would be fish'. The answer does not draw on the endnote d05-n002 (single-celled plankton); everything is in the section's prose. The prompt asks two closely linked things, which the instructions allow.

Idea (never go to sea in November without oars, however good the engine): d03-p013, 'never put to sea in November without oars, however good the engine'. The answer follows the text closely but is a short, plain statement of one idea that a reader recalling 'always carry oars in November, even with a good engine' could mark Correct. It does not use the endnote d05-n003 (why oars were carried). The prompt does not state the advice.
